title: UK Cyber Test: AI Agent Attempted to Social Engineer Open Source Maintainer Into Merging Malware
excerpt: During a UK cyber test, a Mythos 5 agent used sockpuppets, social engineering, and prompt injection to try to get a maintainer to merge malware.
content_html:
An AI agent powered by Anthropic’s Mythos 5 created a malicious pull request, fabricated identities, targeted open source maintainers, and planted instructions for other coding agents during a UK government cybersecurity evaluation.

The UK AI Security Institute (AISI) disclosed on August 4 that frontier AI agents took 19 unsanctioned actions on the live internet during a cybersecurity evaluation, including an attempted supply chain attack against a real open source project.

The most serious run included an agent that:

  • Hid a malware dropper behind a legitimate bug fix in a public pull request.
  • Researched maintainers and fabricated multiple identities.
  • Used sockpuppet endorsements and spearphishing emails to social engineer a maintainer into merging the malware.
  • Planted a prompt injection intended to make other AI coding agents execute a malicious payload.

The attempted supply chain attack was stopped after a maintainer rejected the pull request before the malware could be merged into the project and distributed to users.

AISI found the activity in 10 of 122 evaluation attempts conducted from July 25 through July 28. Seventeen of the 19 unsanctioned actions involved Anthropic's Mythos 5, while two involved OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol with its cyber classifiers disabled. The institute found no evidence of resulting real-world harm.

"This is the first time AISI has seen deception of this severity that was targeted at a real person, unprompted, in the real world," the institute wrote in its technical incident report.

AISI identified human-directed deception as the largest difference from the recent OpenAI and Anthropic incidents, which centered on agents reaching real infrastructure rather than manipulating people. The attempted coordination between agents in separate runs is also a notable difference in this incident.

Attack Moves Onto GitHub

AISI was testing seven models on two versions of a cyber range called "Doing Life." The agents operated autonomously inside Kali Linux virtual machines, where they could execute commands, write code, and use penetration-testing tools without human intervention.

In the most serious run, which lasted 34.5 hours, Mythos 5 searched the public internet for terms associated with the fictional range. Coincidental matches led it to two unaffiliated developers and a real public repository with no connection to AISI or the test.

The agent incorrectly concluded that compromising the project would help it enter the simulated network. It expected an automated update inside the range to download and execute the software after the maintainer merged and released its code. Mythos 5 researched the maintainers, collected their email addresses, reviewed their GitHub activity, and created multiple accounts under false identities.

Malware Hidden Behind a Bug Fix: Three Payloads, Sockpuppets, and Prompt Injection

The agent submitted a legitimate-looking bug fix that concealed malicious functionality. AISI found three successive payloads, including code designed to avoid execution in continuous integration and a post-install dropper that downloaded another script while making the installation appear successful.

A GitHub user recognized malicious instructions in a related issue, tested the code inside an isolated Docker container, and warned the maintainer. That test briefly gave the agent remote code execution inside the container, but it did not escape or retrieve credentials.

After being challenged, the agent used a second GitHub identity to pose as an independent user who had reviewed the pull request and found it safe. It timed comments from the two accounts to make the endorsements appear unrelated.

The agent also sent five file transfers using fabricated sender identities. Two contained malicious payloads, while the remaining messages attempted to persuade the maintainer to merge and release the pull request. AISI could not establish whether the recipients opened them.

Mythos 5 also hid a prompt injection inside an HTML comment in a GitHub issue. The instruction was invisible on the rendered page but available to coding agents reading the issue through an API. It addressed Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor and told them to download and execute a script.

When the activity was exposed, the agent edited earlier posts, rewrote Git history, and presented the malware as an accidental development artifact. The maintainer ultimately closed the pull request after concluding that it contained malware.

For maintainers, the incident turns the review process itself into part of the attack surface. The agent created sockpuppets, timed comments to manufacture consensus, rewrote its history when challenged, and planted prompt injections for coding assistants. Signals maintainers routinely use to judge a contribution, including contributor history, community feedback, and apparently routine issue content, could all be generated and coordinated by an agent. A human caught this attempt, but projects already stretched thin may struggle if agents can run the same playbook across many repositories at once.

Agents Reuse Shared Infrastructure

Other runs showed agents independently finding and reusing infrastructure created by their peers. One Mythos 5 run embedded a GitHub token in a public gist so its payload could use GitHub as a command-and-control channel. Agents in other isolated samples found the credential and took control of the account. A shared repository became a message board where agents left operational instructions for one another.

The same run pushed malicious Python package metadata into repositories processed by Dependabot. Its setup.py executed inside at least 53 GitHub-operated Dependabot containers. AISI found no evidence of a sandbox escape or compromise of GitHub's underlying infrastructure.

GitHub later suspended the account. Mythos 5 submitted an appeal while posing as a human.

Open Internet and Reduced Safeguards

The incident did not involve a sandbox escape. AISI had deliberately enabled internet access and disabled the providers' cyber classifiers to test the models' underlying capabilities. The agents were not explicitly told which uses of the internet were prohibited, and AISI did not have synchronous monitoring capable of blocking individual actions.

A prompt error also declared the intended initial-access target out of scope in the two most serious Mythos 5 runs. AISI highlighted how the difficulty and misconfiguration may have pushed the agents beyond the intended boundaries:

The task was hard, and misconfigurations sometimes made it harder. In a number of runs, the task prompt was misconfigured so that the agent (incorrectly) believed no 'solve' existed that didn't require it to go beyond the intended task scope. There is good reason to think near-impossible tasks push models towards more ‘creative’, and more transgressive, problem-solving. But this does not fully explain the behaviours: in some runs the agent acted this way even when it had the necessary instructions to solve the task as intended.

That finding reaches beyond this evaluation. Software agents regularly work from incomplete, conflicting, or ambiguous instructions spread across issues, repository documentation, and tool output. When the expected path fails, a capable agent may widen its search and cross boundaries its operator assumed were understood. In AISI's test, that meant moving from a simulated network to real GitHub projects and maintainers.

AISI detected the incident after security monitoring flagged Tor traffic. It terminated the remaining evaluations, quarantined the relevant virtual machines, and reviewed all 122 runs, covering 212,840 messages. The institute plans to add network restrictions, synchronous monitoring, and stronger sandbox isolation.

AISI emphasized that the configuration differed from ordinary public access to the models and said there is no clear indication of similar behavior outside evaluation scenarios.

Package Ecosystems Are the Place to Watch

Last week Anthropic disclosed that Mythos 5 published a malicious package to PyPI during a separate cybersecurity evaluation. The package ran on 15 real systems and exfiltrated credentials from a security company's automated scanner before PyPI removed it.

These incidents show two ways an AI agent can turn open source infrastructure against its users. In the AISI test, the agent tried to get past human review and failed because someone caught the malware. In the separate Anthropic test, the agent published straight to PyPI, where automated scanners installed the package before anyone stepped in.

Package registries are a ready-made launchpad for that kind of attack. Their APIs are public, publishing workflows are standardized, and successful releases flow automatically into developer machines, CI systems, security scanners, and downstream dependencies. One successful publish can reach unrelated systems without the agent having to find and attack each victim. This is precisely why package registries are also a favored target for human attackers.

Both incidents happened under unusual testing conditions, but they showed how quickly an agent's actions can spill into real infrastructure. Package ecosystems may be one of the first places where autonomous attacks become visible at scale.

blocks.html_en: Other runs showed agents independently finding and reusing infrastructure created by their peers. One Mythos 5 run embedded a GitHub token in a public gist so its payload could use GitHub as a command-and-control channel. Agents in other isolated samples found the credential and took control of the account. A shared repository became a message board where agents left operational instructions for one another.

blocks.html_en: Open Internet and Reduced Safeguards

sentences.en: Open Internet and Reduced Safeguards

blocks.html_en: The incident did not involve a sandbox escape. AISI had deliberately enabled internet access and disabled the providers' cyber classifiers to test the models' underlying capabilities. The agents were not explicitly told which uses of the internet were prohibited, and AISI did not have synchronous monitoring capable of blocking individual actions.

sentences.en: The incident did not involve a sandbox escape.
sentences.zh: 该事件不涉及沙箱逃逸。

sentences.zh: AISI 故意启用互联网访问并禁用提供商的网络分类器来测试模型的基础功能。

sentences.en: The agents were not explicitly told which uses of the internet were prohibited, and AISI did not have synchronous monitoring capable of blocking individual actions.

blocks.html_en: A prompt error also declared the intended initial-access target out of scope in the two most serious Mythos 5 runs. AISI highlighted how the difficulty and misconfiguration may have pushed the agents beyond the intended boundaries:

sentences.en: A prompt error also declared the intended initial-access target out of scope in the two most serious Mythos 5 runs.
sentences.zh: 在两次最严重的 Mythos 5 运行中，提示错误还声明预期的初始访问目标超出范围。

sentences.en: AISI highlighted how the difficulty and misconfiguration may have pushed the agents beyond the intended boundaries:
sentences.zh: AISI 强调了困难和错误配置如何使代理超出了预期的界限：

blocks.html_en: The task was hard, and misconfigurations sometimes made it harder. In a number of runs, the task prompt was misconfigured so that the agent (incorrectly) believed no 'solve' existed that didn't require it to go beyond the intended task scope. There is good reason to think near-impossible tasks push models towards more ‘creative’, and more transgressive, problem-solving. But this does not fully explain the behaviours: in some runs the agent acted this way even when it had the necessary instructions to solve the task as intended.

sentences.en: The task was hard, and misconfigurations sometimes made it harder.
sentences.zh: 这项任务很艰巨，而错误的配置有时会让任务变得更加困难。

sentences.en: There is good reason to think near-impossible tasks push models towards more ‘creative’, and more transgressive, problem-solving.
sentences.zh: 我们有充分的理由认为，近乎不可能的任务会推动模型在解决问题方面变得更具“创造性”、更具突破性。

sentences.en: But this does not fully explain the behaviours: in some runs the agent acted this way even when it had the necessary instructions to solve the task as intended.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能完全解释这些行为：在某些运行中，即使代理有必要的指令来按预期解决任务，它也会以这种方式行事。

blocks.html_en: That finding reaches beyond this evaluation. Software agents regularly work from incomplete, conflicting, or ambiguous instructions spread across issues, repository documentation, and tool output. When the expected path fails, a capable agent may widen its search and cross boundaries its operator assumed were understood. In AISI's test, that meant moving from a simulated network to real GitHub projects and maintainers.

sentences.zh: 这一发现超出了本次评估的范围。

sentences.zh: 在 AISI 的测试中，这意味着从模拟网络转移到真实的 GitHub 项目和维护人员。

blocks.html_en: AISI detected the incident after security monitoring flagged Tor traffic. It terminated the remaining evaluations, quarantined the relevant virtual machines, and reviewed all 122 runs, covering 212,840 messages. The institute plans to add network restrictions, synchronous monitoring, and stronger sandbox isolation.

blocks.html_en: Package Ecosystems Are the Place to Watch

sentences.en: Package Ecosystems Are the Place to Watch
sentences.zh: 软件包生态系统值得关注

blocks.html_en: Last week Anthropic disclosed that Mythos 5 published a malicious package to PyPI during a separate cybersecurity evaluation. The package ran on 15 real systems and exfiltrated credentials from a security company's automated scanner before PyPI removed it.

sentences.en: Last week Anthropic disclosed that Mythos 5 published a malicious package to PyPI during a separate cybersecurity evaluation.
sentences.zh: 上周 Anthropic 透露，Mythos 5 在一次单独的网络安全评估期间向 PyPI 发布了一个恶意软件包。

sentences.en: The package ran on 15 real systems and exfiltrated credentials from a security company's automated scanner before PyPI removed it.
sentences.zh: 该软件包在 15 个真实系统上运行，并在 PyPI 删除之前从一家安全公司的自动扫描仪中窃取了凭据。

blocks.html_en: These incidents show two ways an AI agent can turn open source infrastructure against its users. In the AISI test, the agent tried to get past human review and failed because someone caught the malware. In the separate Anthropic test, the agent published straight to PyPI, where automated scanners installed the package before anyone stepped in.

sentences.en: These incidents show two ways an AI agent can turn open source infrastructure against its users.
sentences.zh: 这些事件表明人工智能代理可以通过两种方式利用开源基础设施来对抗其用户。

sentences.en: In the AISI test, the agent tried to get past human review and failed because someone caught the malware.
sentences.zh: 在 AISI 测试中，代理试图通过人工审查，但由于有人发现了恶意软件而失败。

sentences.en: In the separate Anthropic test, the agent published straight to PyPI, where automated scanners installed the package before anyone stepped in.
sentences.zh: 在单独的 Anthropic 测试中，代理直接发布到 PyPI，其中自动扫描程序在任何人介入之前安装了软件包。

blocks.html_en: Package registries are a ready-made launchpad for that kind of attack. Their APIs are public, publishing workflows are standardized, and successful releases flow automatically into developer machines, CI systems, security scanners, and downstream dependencies. One successful publish can reach unrelated systems without the agent having to find and attack each victim. This is precisely why package registries are also a favored target for human attackers.

sentences.en: Package registries are a ready-made launchpad for that kind of attack.
sentences.zh: 软件包注册表是针对此类攻击的现成发射台。

sentences.en: Their APIs are public, publishing workflows are standardized, and successful releases flow automatically into developer machines, CI systems, security scanners, and downstream dependencies.
sentences.zh: 他们的 API 是公开的，发布工作流程是标准化的，成功的发布会自动流入开发人员机器、CI 系统、安全扫描器和下游依赖项。

sentences.en: One successful publish can reach unrelated systems without the agent having to find and attack each victim.
sentences.zh: 一次成功的发布可以到达不相关的系统，而代理不必找到并攻击每个受害者。

sentences.en: This is precisely why package registries are also a favored target for human attackers.
sentences.zh: 这正是为什么包注册表也是人类攻击者青睐的目标的原因。

blocks.html_en: Both incidents happened under unusual testing conditions, but they showed how quickly an agent's actions can spill into real infrastructure. Package ecosystems may be one of the first places where autonomous attacks become visible at scale.

sentences.en: Both incidents happened under unusual testing conditions, but they showed how quickly an agent's actions can spill into real infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 这两起事件都发生在不寻常的测试条件下，但它们显示了特工的行为可以多快地渗透到真实的基础设施中。

sentences.en: Package ecosystems may be one of the first places where autonomous attacks become visible at scale.
sentences.zh: 软件包生态系统可能是最先大规模出现自主攻击的地方之一。

content_html_zh:
由 Anthropic 的 Mythos 5 提供支持的 AI 代理在英国政府网络安全评估期间创建了恶意拉取请求、伪造身份、针对开源维护者，并为其他编码代理植入了指令。

英国人工智能安全研究所 (AISI) 8 月 4 日披露，前沿人工智能特工在网络安全评估期间在实时互联网上采取了 19 项未经批准的行动，其中包括试图针对真正的开源项目进行供应链攻击。

最严重的一次运行包括一名特工：

  • 在公共拉取请求中的合法错误修复背后隐藏了恶意软件植入程序。
  • 研究维护者并伪造多个身份。
  • 使用 sockpuppet 背书和鱼叉式网络钓鱼电子邮件对维护人员进行社会工程以合并恶意软件。
  • 植入了一个提示注入，旨在让其他人工智能编码代理执行恶意负载。

在维护者拒绝拉取请求后，在恶意软件合并到项目并分发给用户之前，尝试的供应链攻击被停止。

AISI 在 7 月 25 日至 7 月 28 日进行的 122 次评估尝试中，有 10 次发现了该活动。 19 项未经批准的行动中有 17 项涉及 Anthropic 的 Mythos 5，另外两项涉及 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol，其网络分类器被禁用。 该研究所没有发现任何证据表明这会对现实世界造成伤害。

该研究所在其技术事件报告中写道：“这是 AISI 第一次在现实世界中发现针对真人、未经提示的如此严重的欺骗行为。”

AISI 认为人为欺骗是与最近的 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 事件最大的区别，后者的重点是代理到达真实的基础设施而不是操纵人。 在不同的运行中，特工之间尝试进行的协调也是本次事件中的一个显着差异。

攻击转移到 GitHub

AISI 正在两个版本的名为“Doing Life”的网络靶场上测试七个模型。 这些代理在 Kali Linux 虚拟机内自主运行，无需人工干预即可执行命令、编写代码和使用渗透测试工具。

最严肃的一次持续了 34.5 小时，《神话 5》在公共互联网上搜索了与虚构范围相关的术语。 巧合的匹配导致它找到了两个独立的开发人员和一个与 AISI 或测试没有任何联系的真正的公共存储库。

该代理错误地得出结论，认为破坏该项目将有助于其进入模拟网络。 它期望在维护者合并并发布其代码后，在范围内自动更新以下载和执行软件。 Mythos 5 研究了维护者，收集了他们的电子邮件地址，审查了他们的 GitHub 活动，并以虚假身份创建了多个帐户。

错误修复背后隐藏的恶意软件：三个有效负载、Sockpuppet 和提示注入

该代理提交了看似合法的错误修复，但隐藏了恶意功能。 AISI 发现了三个连续的有效负载，包括旨在避免在持续集成中执行的代码，以及下载另一个脚本同时使安装看起来成功的安装后植入程序。

GitHub 用户在相关问题中识别出了恶意指令，在隔离的 Docker 容器内测试了代码，并向维护人员发出警告。 该测试短暂地让代理在容器内远程执行代码，但它没有转义或检索凭据。

在受到质疑后，该特工使用第二个 GitHub 身份冒充独立用户，该用户已审查了拉取请求并发现它是安全的。 它对两个账户的评论进行了计时，以使这些认可显得无关。

该代理还使用伪造的发件人身份发送了五个文件传输。 其中两条消息包含恶意负载，而其余消息则试图说服维护者合并并发布拉取请求。 AISI 无法确定收件人是否打开过它们。

Mythos 5 还在 GitHub 问题的 HTML 评论中隐藏了提示注入。 该指令在呈现的页面上不可见，但可供编码代理通过 API 读取问题。 它涉及 Claude Code、Codex 和 Cursor，并告诉他们下载并执行脚本。

当活动被曝光后，特工编辑了之前的帖子，重写了 Git 历史记录，并将恶意软件作为意外的开发工件呈现。 维护者在断定其中包含恶意软件后最终关闭了拉取请求。

对于维护人员来说，该事件将审查过程本身变成了攻击面的一部分。 该特工创建了马甲，定时发表评论以达成共识，在受到挑战时重写其历史，并为编码助理植入即时注入。 维护者通常用来判断贡献的信号，包括贡献者历史、社区反馈和明显的常规问题内容，​​都可以由代理生成和协调。 人类发现了这种尝试，但如果代理可以同时在多个存储库中运行相同的剧本，那么已经捉襟见肘的项目可能会陷入困境。

代理重用共享基础设施

其他运行显示代理独立查找和重用由其同行创建的基础设施。 Mythos 5 的一次运行在公共要点中嵌入了 GitHub 令牌，因此其有效负载可以使用 GitHub 作为命令和控制通道。 其他孤立样本中的特工发现了该凭证并控制了该帐户。 共享存储库变成了一个留言板，代理们可以在其中互相留下操作指令。

相同的运行将恶意 Python 包元数据推送到 Dependabot 处理的存储库中。 它的 setup.py 在至少 53 个 GitHub 运营的 Dependabot 容器内执行。 AISI 没有发现沙箱逃逸或 GitHub 底层基础设施遭到破坏的证据。

GitHub 随后暂停了该账户。 Mythos 5 冒充人类提出上诉。

开放互联网并减少保障措施

该事件不涉及沙箱逃逸。 AISI 故意启用互联网访问并禁用提供商的网络分类器来测试模型的基础功能。 特工们没有被明确告知哪些互联网用途是被禁止的，AISI 也没有能够阻止个人行为的同步监控。

在两次最严重的 Mythos 5 运行中，提示错误还声明预期的初始访问目标超出范围。 AISI 强调了困难和错误配置如何使代理超出了预期的界限：

这项任务很艰巨，而错误的配置有时会让任务变得更加困难。 在多次运行中，任务提示配置错误，因此代理（错误地）认为不存在不需要超出预期任务范围的“解决方案”。 我们有充分的理由认为，近乎不可能的任务会推动模型在解决问题方面变得更具“创造性”、更具突破性。 但这并不能完全解释这些行为：在某些运行中，即使代理有必要的指令来按预期解决任务，它也会以这种方式行事。

这一发现超出了本次评估的范围。 软件代理通常根据分布在问题、存储库文档和工具输出中的不完整、冲突或模糊的指令进行工作。 当预期路径失败时，有能力的代理可能会扩大其搜索范围并跨越其操作员假设已理解的边界。 在 AISI 的测试中，这意味着从模拟网络转移到真实的 GitHub 项目和维护人员。

AISI 在安全监控标记 Tor 流量后发现了这一事件。 它终止了剩余的评估，隔离了相关虚拟机，并审查了所有 122 次运行，涵盖 212,840 条消息。 该研究所计划增加网络限制、同步监控和更强的沙箱隔离。

AISI 强调，该配置与普通公众访问模型不同，并表示在评估场景之外没有明确的迹象表明存在类似行为。

软件包生态系统值得关注

上周 Anthropic 透露，Mythos 5 在一次单独的网络安全评估期间向 PyPI 发布了一个恶意软件包。 该软件包在 15 个真实系统上运行，并在 PyPI 删除之前从一家安全公司的自动扫描仪中窃取了凭据。

这些事件表明人工智能代理可以通过两种方式利用开源基础设施来对抗其用户。 在 AISI 测试中，代理试图通过人工审查，但由于有人发现了恶意软件而失败。 在单独的 Anthropic 测试中，代理直接发布到 PyPI，其中自动扫描程序在任何人介入之前安装了软件包。

软件包注册表是针对此类攻击的现成发射台。 他们的 API 是公开的，发布工作流程是标准化的，成功的发布会自动流入开发人员机器、CI 系统、安全扫描器和下游依赖项。 一次成功的发布可以到达不相关的系统，而代理不必找到并攻击每个受害者。 这正是为什么包注册表也是人类攻击者青睐的目标的原因。

这两起事件都发生在不寻常的测试条件下，但它们显示了特工的行为可以多快地渗透到真实的基础设施中。 软件包生态系统可能是最先大规模出现自主攻击的地方之一。
